text:
tara: heads up — we hit a weird case in staging where two different service accounts ended up with the same human-readable name and the quota routing picked the wrong project/limit.
kevin: ugh, are those display-name collisions or internal ids?
mike: display-name collisions. both SA objects had `display_name: training-worker` after an import. internal ids differ.
jess: important to call out: console UX currently shows display name top-level in route selection, so operators easily pick the wrong one.
tara: right. the routing code prefers `name` header if present, then falls back to `display_name` for some telemetry labels — that's how we ended up mapping tokens to the wrong quota bucket.
kevin: can you paste the header blob?
mike: sure — example incoming request: 
```
Authorization: Bearer tok_abc123
X-Redwood-Auth: sa:proj-42:training-worker
X-Redwood-SA-Display: training-worker
```
mike: routing used `X-Redwood-SA-Display` when `X-Redwood-Auth` parsing failed for an older token format.
kevin: parsing failed because the token was minted pre-migration?
tara: yes, pre-migration ephemeral tokens lack the `sa:proj` prefix.
ops-sheriff: reaction :eyes: — so quota attribution went to the first matching display name in the routing table?
jess: exactly. our map is keyed by display name in the in-memory cache if the id isn't present. order is nondeterministic after import.
kevin: we shouldn't be using display name for any authoritative mapping. that's high risk.
mike: agreed. short-term fixes: 1) prefer canonical id when present, 2) add deterministic tie-breaker (alphabetical org+id) in cache, 3) emit a telemetry event when display-name fallback happens.
tara: +1 on telemetry. we need a clear signal to find customer-impact cases. what event fields do we want?
kevin: event: `auth.mapping.fallback`; fields: token_format, resolved_by (display|id), chosen_key, candidates_count, request_region. keep it small.
ops-sheriff: and include `console_correlation_id` if present so support can trace.
jess: console UX fix: show primary identifier (project+id) and then show display name as secondary. also gray out duplicates with a tooltip: "Duplicate display name — prefer id".
kevin: rollout plan: patch runtime to log fallback events + deterministic tie-breaker, enable for canary (10% traffic) for 48h, then escalate to 100% if no anomalies.
mike: canary config: env var `AUTH_MAPPING_CANARY=0.1` and `AUTH_MAPPING_VERBOSE=true` to emit extra debug logs.
tara: ops/sre: can you wire a dashboard? metrics we want: fallback_rate by org, top conflicting display names, affected_projects_count, latency delta when fallback used.
ops-sheriff: will add a grafana panel and a small alert: if fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 1h -> page. also add a sparse log-sampling stream to `#incidents` during canary.
kevin: what about quota enforcement? if routing changes to id-first, will quotas shift mid-flight and throttle customers unexpectedly?
jess: we can add a soft-enforcement window: for 7 days after switching to id-first, apply new quota only for new tokens; existing tokens keep previous mapping. implementation: attach `quota_source_version` to token metadata.
mike: that requires token metadata migration for persisted tokens — doable. we should also provide a UI toggle per-org to opt into early enforcement for testing partners.
tara: good call. also, we need a migration-runner to detect imported SAs with duplicate display names and auto-suffix them with ` (imported-<shortid>)` in the console, but only if the org opts in.
kevin: don't auto-rename without consent. maybe mark them as "name conflict: confirm rename" in the console and offer bulk rename tool.
ops-sheriff: telemetry: add a weekly report for PMs that lists top-10 display-name conflicts by customer impact (quota hits, errors).
jess: PR checklist items: unit tests for parser fallback, integration test that simulates imported duplicate names, console mock showing conflict banner, and an ops migration runbook.
mike: I'll open a PR with the runtime changes and test vectors.
tara: assign to @kevin for canary config and to @ops-sheriff for dashboards/runbook.
ops-sheriff: assigned, will sync with oncall before we flip 10% -> 100%.
infra-bot: deploy queued — build/7891 to staging.
kevin: one more: ensure metrics include `route_version` so we can rollback precise changes.
tara: ack. thanks everyone, let's track in the RFC thread and loop in product for the customer-impact report. :thumbsup:
